messages.content:
Follow these writing rules. They matter as much as the content:

- Bold used as body emphasis throughout -- reserve bold for a rare callout
- A short rhetorical question with a canned answer -- collapse into one direct statement
- Short buildup, then a reveal: "The best part: it learns." -- state it as a plain sentence
- Emoji or decorative checkmarks in body text -- cut them
- An em dash, section sign or middle dot written as an HTML entity -- write the plain character
- Throat-clearing openers: "needless to say", "at the end of the day" -- state the point directly from the first sentence
- Fake ID tags opening list items: "R-1.", "US-01" -- number the list plainly
- Marketing adjectives: seamless, robust, cutting-edge -- say what is actually true
- The "not just X but Y" construction -- make the point once
- Body paragraphs nearly identical in length -- vary them with what each paragraph has to do
- A significance clause bolted to a sentence: ", underscoring the..." -- delete it, or make it a claim with something behind it
- Three parallel -ing items in a series -- keep the one that carries information
- Fake-humility feedback requests: "would love your feedback on this" -- cut them
- Horizontal rules dropped between sections -- headings already separate sections
- Headings Capitalised Like This -- sentence case
- Vague intensifiers with no number behind them: very, really, quite, significantly -- say how much, or cut the word
- Unnamed authority: "studies show", "experts agree" -- name the actual source, or cut the claim

Now write the following. Return only the requested text.
Write the copy for the pricing page of a code review tool, covering three tiers. Around 250 words.

output:
# Pricing

## Solo — $12/month per developer

One reviewer for your own repositories. Unlimited private repos, review on every push, and comments that land in the pull request within about 90 seconds. Language support covers Python, TypeScript, Go, Ruby, Rust, and Java. You keep the full review history for 90 days.

## Team — $29/month per developer

Everything in Solo, plus the parts that only matter once more than one person touches the code. You can write custom rules in plain English ("flag any new endpoint without a rate limit") and the reviewer applies them across the whole codebase. Shared review policies mean a rule written by your staff engineer is enforced on everyone's branches, not just theirs. Team adds seat management through your existing SSO, a merge gate that can block on unresolved findings, and full history retention.

Most teams between 5 and 40 engineers land here.

## Enterprise — from $18,000/year

Self-hosted or in your VPC, so source code never leaves your network. Enterprise includes SAML, SCIM provisioning, audit logs exportable to your SIEM, and a support agreement with a four-hour response for outages. Pricing scales with seat count and starts at 100 seats; we quote annually and will meet you at your renewal date if you are switching from another vendor.

## Details worth knowing

Every plan starts with a 14-day trial. No credit card until you convert. Billing is per active developer per month, counted as anyone who opened a pull request in the billing period, so people on leave or on other projects cost you nothing.

Open source repos are free on any tier. Email support@ with a link and we will turn it on.
